newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS-Gasoline stocks down in strong seasonal draw.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Gasoline stocks down in strong seasonal draw.

text.p: In keeping with the season, gasoline inventories were drawn down and heating oil stocks built up last week as retailers stocked up for holiday driving and refiners girded for colder weather, analysts said.

U.S. refineries reported a net 3.83 million barrel draw in gasoline and 3.59 million barrel build in distillate stocks, which includes heating oil, American Petroleum Institute said Tuesday in its weekly petroleum stocks report.
Under pressure to boost heating oil supplies, refineries were running at a frantic 94 percent of capacity, API said.

"Even though the summer driving season is over, late November and December are historically the second highest period of (gasoline) demand. Storage may be moving to secondary stocks," said Gerald Samuels of ARB Oil.
Based on the build, implied gasoline demand stood at 8.4 million barrels per day for the second straight week.

"That's more of a June or an August-type demand number," said Peter Beutel, an energy analyst with Cameron Hanover in Bronxville, New York. "You normally get a tiny increase during the autumn foliage season, but usually less than 150,000 barrels or so," he said.

The trade group said refiners nationwide had 186.02 million barrels of gasoline on hand at October 25, down 3.83 million barrels from the prior week and 10.67 million barrels shy of inventory levels in the same week last year.
The draw was fueled by net 2.72 million net reduction in stocks on hand at PADD I East Coast refineries, API said.
Production yields were unchanged on the week, with a typical barrel of crude oil yielding 26.6 percent distillates and 53.3 percent gasoline, analysts said.

With refiners operating at 93.1 percent of capacity in PADD I, up 10.2 percentage points from the prior week, heating oil stocks rose a net 2.82 million barrels on the East Coast as additional stocks were pumped into primary storage by refiners in the region, analysts said.
Nationwide, distillate inventories ended the week at 117.89 million barrels, or 11.89 million barrels short of stocks on hand in the same week last year, API said.

Analysts had forecast a 1.9 million barrel build in distillate stocks, and the bearish API estimate sent NYMEX November heating oil prices tumbling to 68.72 cents a gallon, down 1.11 cent in ACCESS after-hours trade.
November unleaded gasoline was bid 69.05 cents a gallon, asked 69.25 cents after closing the earlier floor session down 1.20 cents at 69.10 cents a gallon.
December crude oil futures were bid $24.15 a barrel, asked $24.20 a barrel after closing off 51 cents at $24.34 a barrel in the floor session.
